NDA-covered · industry-labeled · Managed Nov to Dec 2025 · Islamabad-based engagement

Showing what makes a boutique hotel worth visiting

I planned and published the hotel’s organic social content, keeping the look and tone consistent with the wider marketing team.

My role

I managed the organic calendar and daily publishing, with direction and approvals from the marketing head. A separate team handled paid ads.

Sector

Hospitality · Boutique hotel

Status

Case study / reported evidence

Topics

Hospitality · Organic content · Team delivery

01 / Starting point

The challenge

The hotel needed regular content that felt welcoming and premium without sounding like an endless list of offers. I was responsible for organic content while a separate team ran ads.

The insight

People want to picture themselves staying somewhere. The small details, the rooms, the atmosphere and the experience matter more than another generic promotion.

02 / The approach

The plan

  • Focus posts on atmosphere, rooms and the guest experience.
  • Keep a consistent look and publishing schedule that fits the hotel’s brand.
  • Report organic results separately from paid activity so it is clear what my work covered.
03 / Execution

Make the rhythm visible.

The calendar

I planned the posts for November and December, focusing on the spaces, mood and details that made the hotel appealing.

Working with the team

I followed the marketing head’s direction and kept content, feedback and approvals organized.

Publishing

I handled organic posting throughout the period while a different team managed the Meta ads.

Reporting

I reviewed the account numbers and made it clear which views came from ads. Booking data was not available.

06 / Selected proof

A closer look at the work.

These examples include dates and sources so you can see what they show and what they do not.

04 / Results

Evidence with the label still attached.

The supplied Meta screenshots for 13 November to 13 December 2025 show 22,182 Instagram views (9,368 organic; 12,814 from ads), and 150,509 Facebook views (6,986 organic; 143,523 from ads). Figures describe overall account distribution while paid campaigns were managed separately. Naqash owned organic calendar and posting; bookings and commercial impact were not supplied.

05 / Reflection

What stays after the campaign?

The project taught me how to keep a hospitality brand consistent while working within an established marketing team. It also reinforced why organic and paid results need to be reported separately.

Credits
My contribution: organic content planning and publishing. Paid ads were managed by another team.
